name: com.forwardsmith/forwardsmith
title: Forwardsmith
description: Read-only desk for buyers and assistants: offer, prices, fit check, readiness scan, intake draft.

tools.name: get_offers
tools.description: Returns the three ways to start with Forwardsmith (Information Flow Mapping Session, FDE Build Sprint, FDE 30-60-90 engagement) with duration, starting price as a number in EUR excl. VAT, what it delivers, what is not included, the ownership statement and a list of things the site does not publish, so you can say so instead of guessing. Prices are starting prices, not quotes. Please cite the URL.

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: get_approach
tools.description: Returns how a forward-deployed engineer of Forwardsmith works: Map, Build, Hand over; the five stations of the method and its golden rule; the six kinds of work; the eight points that belong in a statement of work; what must be ready before the start; and the handover test.

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Deterministic fit check with nine yes/no signals taken from the published article on when an FDE fits and when it does not. Returns one of: fits, start_with_mapping, not_clear_yet, wait, something_else_fits_better, each with the sentence from the site it is based on. It also says when another kind of supplier is the simpler choice. Ask the person; do not guess the signals.

signals.description: All nine yes/no signals, each true or false. Ask the person; do not guess. Three or four of signs 1-4 give fits.

one_process_with_owner.description: Sign 1 of the article: there is one process with an owner who can say what a good result is and has the authority to decide.

knowledge_with_people.description: Sign 2: the knowledge (exceptions, rules of thumb, red lines) sits with your people, not on paper.

runs_in_own_environment.description: Sign 3: it has to run in your own environment (own cloud, VPC or on-premises) and talk to your existing systems.

want_to_carry_on_yourselves.description: Sign 4: you want to carry on yourselves afterwards; code, configuration, tests and documentation have to be yours.

experts_and_access_available.description: The people who do the work and the systems it happens in can be made available to the engineer now. false leads to the verdict wait.

sharp_specification.description: You already know exactly what has to be built and how to test it. true leads to something_else_fits_better (build capacity is the simpler choice).

standard_product_covers_it.description: Your process does not differ from anyone else's and a standard package exists for it. true leads to something_else_fits_better.

only_independent_benchmark.description: All you want is an independent benchmark of models or agents. true leads to something_else_fits_better.

wants_to_buy_model_or_platform.description: You mainly want to buy a model or a platform; Forwardsmith does not resell those. true leads to something_else_fits_better.

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: run_readiness_scan
tools.description: Runs the same six-question FDE Readiness Scan as the page on forwardsmith.com, with the same scoring. Returns the score, the recommended starting point with its starting price, what is already in place and what to prepare. Self-assessment.

process.description: Which process would you start with?

history.description: How many historical cases with a known outcome can you pull?

sensitivity.description: How sensitive is the data in these cases?

redlines.description: Are there hard red-line rules the system must never break?

models.description: How do you use AI models or tools in this process today?

volume.description: What monthly volume do you want this process to handle?

answers.description: The six answers of the FDE Readiness Scan, one option id per question, all six required (the same questions as the scan page).

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: scope_mapping_session
tools.description: Takes one process as 2-20 steps and returns per step whether it is handled by code (MCP/API), by a model (and on which route) or by a person, whether a redaction gate comes first and whether human approval is needed. Fixed rule table from the published method; no model is called. A preview of what the Information Flow Mapping Session does with your team, not a design. Describe steps in general words; no personal data.

process_name.description: Short name of the process in general words (3-160 characters). No personal data.

steps.description: The steps of the process in order, 2 to 20. Each step is routed to code, a model or a person.

name.description: What happens in this step, in general words (2-120 characters). No personal data.

kind.description: What the step does. Handled by code: fetch_record, calculate, write_record, notify. Handled by a model: classify, extract, summarise, draft_text (Route A candidate), judge_edge_case (Route B candidate). Handled by a person: decide.

personal_data.description: true when the step handles personal data; for a model step a redaction gate then comes first. Default false.

external_effect.description: true when the step pays, rejects, books or sends something outside the organisation; a step not taken by a person then needs human approval. Default false.

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: estimate_engagement
tools.description: Adds up the published starting prices for a chosen path of one to three steps (mapping, sprint, fde). Returns the lines, the sum as a lower bound in EUR excl. VAT, what is not included and what is not published. No discounts, no new prices.

path.description: One to three different steps in the order you would take them: mapping (Information Flow Mapping Session), sprint (FDE Build Sprint), fde (FDE 30-60-90 engagement).

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).

tools.name: prepare_intake_request
tools.description: Turns what you learned into a ready-to-send intake request: a brief in ten numbered lines, a link that opens the intake form with the message already filled in, and (once delivery to the inbox is confirmed) an e-mail to contact@forwardsmith.com. It sends nothing and stores nothing: the person reads the text, adds name and work e-mail and sends it. Do not put names, e-mail addresses or phone numbers in any field; the tool refuses them.

process.description: Which process should work, in general words (10-600 characters). Line 1 of the brief.

problem.description: What goes wrong today (10-600 characters). Line 2 of the brief.

owner_role.description: Role of the process owner, not a name (up to 120 characters).

systems.description: Systems the process runs in, for example ERP, CRM, DMS or ticketing (up to 300 characters).

environment.description: Where the solution has to run: own_cloud, vpc, on_premises or undecided (not decided yet).

data_sensitivity.description: How sensitive the data is: low, medium, high-classified (high, classified per field) or high-unclear (high, not yet classified).

known_outcome_cases.description: How many historical cases with a known outcome can be pulled: lt50 (fewer than 50), 50-200, 200-1000, gt1000 (more than 1,000) or unknown.

red_lines.description: Red lines: what the system must never do (up to 400 characters).

why_now.description: Why this matters now (up to 300 characters).

preferred_start.description: Preferred starting point: mapping, sprint, fde or unsure (default).

process.description: Which process would you start with?

history.description: How many historical cases with a known outcome can you pull?

sensitivity.description: How sensitive is the data in these cases?

redlines.description: Are there hard red-line rules the system must never break?

models.description: How do you use AI models or tools in this process today?

volume.description: What monthly volume do you want this process to handle?

scan_answers.description: Optional: the six readiness-scan answers, the same format as answers in run_readiness_scan. Adds the score and the recommended start as line 10 of the brief.

lang.description: Language of the answer: en (English, default) or nl (Dutch).
